sources.title: Biodiversity Net Gain
sources.verified_claim: Enfield states most major and minor development proposals subject to BNG must provide at least 10% biodiversity net gain and specific validation information; BNG is an application requirement, not evidence of parcel development potential.

sources.title: Sustainable drainage systems
sources.verified_claim: Enfield, as Lead Local Flood Authority and statutory consultee, requires a sustainable drainage strategy for planning applications and a flood risk assessment where development is in a flood-risk area.

sources.title: Climate change and biodiversity
sources.verified_claim: Enfield's Blue and Green Strategy guides blue/green infrastructure and development, including flood reduction, biodiversity, woodland, wetlands, walking and cycling ambitions; it remains borough-level policy context.

sources.title: Biodiversity Net Gain
sources.verified_claim: Havering states major and small-site applications subject to BNG must deliver at least 10% net gain secured for at least 30 years, in addition to existing ecological protections.

sources.title: Submit or pay for a planning application
sources.verified_claim: Lambeth states where Section 106 secures a post-approval Biodiversity Gain Plan, long-term BNG monitoring fees may apply over 30 years, with a stated starting point for smaller schemes; this is a delivery obligation, not a parcel score.

sources.title: Green Roots Fund
sources.verified_claim: City Hall's Green Roots Fund provides £10,000 to £500,000 grants for green and blue infrastructure with at least 10% match funding; programme availability does not establish an award to a sample parcel.

sources.title: Green Roots Fund prospectus
sources.verified_claim: The prospectus sets eligibility, 10% match-funding rules, project-duration limits and a 14 January 2027 Round 4 deadline; application eligibility is not treated as funding award or parcel applicability.

sources.title: Understanding biodiversity net gain
sources.verified_claim: National BNG guidance was updated on 14 July 2026 and notes a rule change taking effect 6 August 2026 for developments of 0.2 hectares or below; national rules are retained as policy context pending exact parcel characteristics.
